newsitem.title: TURKEY: Denktash meets Turk president on eve of U.N. talks.
newsitem.headline: Denktash meets Turk president on eve of U.N. talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash arrived in Ankara on Friday for talks with Turkish leaders about a U.N.-sponsored meeting with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides next week.

Old rivals Denktash and Clerides are to meet in upstate New York from July 9-13 in a tentative bid to end the division of Cyprus. The island has been split since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
Denktash said on Thursday he would definitely attend the talks despite threatening this week to pull out if any document is put on the table before he has been informed of its contents.
After meeting with Turkey's president Suleyman Demirel, Denktash said he was travelling to New York with good intentions.
"I'm going in order to understand the other side's ideas with sincerity," Anatolian news agency quoted Denktash as saying.
Denktash was to meet Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz and Foreign Minister Ismail Cem later on his one-day visit.
Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state that is recognised only by Ankara. Clerides leads the Greek Cypriot administration, regarded abroad as the island's only government.
